strengths: Well-motivated frequency decomposition strategy with clear visualization demonstrating that moiré patterns concentrate in high-frequency while color distortions appear in low-frequency components

Comprehensive experimental validation including comparisons against 8 demoiréing methods and 5 general restoration models, with strong results on FHDMi (PSNR 25.26, SSIM 0.8518) and competitive results on UHDM
Practical efficiency with only 6.065M parameters and 2.49 TFLOPS for 4K processing, significantly outperforming larger baselines while maintaining performance
Intelligent dual-branch training strategy (crop for high-frequency, resize for low-frequency) well-justified by frequency component properties and validated by ~6 dB PSNR improvement
Substantial empirical advantage over wavelet-based methods (25.26 vs 13.32 PSNR against Haar), demonstrating genuine superiority of the proposed decomposition
Extensive ablation studies validating each component's contribution and establishing the importance of the dual-branch approach
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (particularly Fig. 2) and sufficient implementation details for reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited novelty at the component level: the frequency decomposition kernel is adapted from existing work [37], and SA-CA combines standard modules (RDDB, channel attention, gated FFN). Ablations show minimal impact from some components (Table 6), questioning their necessity

Insufficient analysis of the learnable FCT module: marginal empirical improvements (0.13 PSNR/0.004 SSIM) over fixed variant, unclear what is being learned, and limited justification for the added complexity
Lack of theoretical grounding: why the specific kernel (Eq. 1) is optimal for moiré separation is not justified; the connection to diffusion priors is mentioned but unexplained
Limited generalization analysis: only tested on FHDMi and UHDM with no cross-dataset evaluation; second-best PSNR on UHDM (22.22 vs 22.42) suggests method may be specialized to these datasets
Incomplete justification of two-stage training: why separate pre-training of branches is necessary is not explored; Table 4 shows end-to-end fails but lacks mechanistic explanation
Missing ablations and analysis: no study of deep supervision necessity, sensitivity to hyperparameters, crop-to-inference translation, boundary effects, or failure modes
Presentation issues: informal language ('awesome benefits'), grammatical errors ('reals'), typos ('benifits'), redundancy between sections, and blank code repository URL
Architectural details under-specified: exact channel numbers and depth specifications for transformer layers only partially provided (N values), limiting reproducibility details
